name: How to Read the Evidence in This Volume
title: How to Read the Evidence in This Volume
answer: Every idea in this volume carries an evidence label that shows whether it has been tested or is a sensible practice not yet studied. Most ideas are labeled Practice because generative AI reached schools recently and careful research takes years. This matters because it tells school leaders, teachers and parents how much caution to apply before trusting any single idea.

crumbs.name: What AI Can and Cannot Do

sections.body: The volume uses evidence labels to sort its 300 ideas into those that have been tested and those that are sensible practice without study behind them. Both kinds of ideas are included, but the label signals that they deserve different levels of caution. Most ideas fall under the Practice label, which the book presents honestly rather than as something to hide. The reason is timing: generative AI arrived in schools in late 2022, and careful research takes years to produce. The practical consequence is that most current AI use in schools rests on informed judgment rather than proven method, and it should be treated that way.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The book recommends three habits for anyone using these ideas in a school. First, start small and measure something that matters, such as learning, time saved or attendance, rather than just whether people liked the tool, with Chapter 4 explaining how. Second, favor ideas where the risk is low if the idea turns out not to work, such as drafting a newsletter, over ideas where a mistake could hurt a child, such as flagging students for discipline. Third, check back, because the research is moving fast and some labels in the volume may change soon after publication. The text does not give separate guidance by grade band for this idea.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels this idea as a way of reading evidence rather than as a finding in itself, and it states that most of the 300 ideas in the volume carry the Practice label. It explains that this is not a weakness to hide, because generative AI reached schools in late 2022 and careful research takes years. Figure 1.7 defines the four labels and shows how many ideas carry each. The text does not report a study, figure or finding beyond that count, so the guidance here rests on the book's own labeling scheme and on practice rather than on research results.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets clear limits on how much confidence any idea deserves. Because most ideas are labeled Practice, they should be treated as informed judgment rather than proven method. The book asks readers to prefer low risk ideas, such as drafting a newsletter, over ideas where a mistake could hurt a child, such as flagging students for discipline. It also warns that labels may change soon after publication as research moves fast, so readers should check back. The decisions about what to try, what to measure and where a mistake could harm a student stay with the people in the school, not with the label itself.
